subject: Error in writing model where transformed parameters computed based on previous value of variable

messages.author: cff2d4d993e62c5e
messages.subject: Error in writing model where transformed parameters computed based on previous value of variable
parts:
I am trying to write a stan model code like this:
stanmodelcode <- "
data {
int<lower=0> M;
int<lower=0> N1;
int<lower=0> Y[M];
}

parameters {
real<lower=0.00001> lambda;
}

transformed parameters {
N2 = N1-Y[1];
}

model {
lambda ~ uniform(0,1);
Y[1] ~ binomial(N1, lambda);
Y[2] ~ binomial(N2, lambda);
}
"
Here in the model our Y[2] is generated from binomial(N2, lambda) and N2 is N1-Y[1]. So how can I write the code for this such type of problems.

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Error in writing model where transformed parameters computed based on previous value of variable
parts:
Hi Arun, 

I'm not sure if I understand what you're trying to do from a modeling perspective. Can you can say a bit more about what you're working on? It looks like you're trying to estimate N2 but at the same time it's a deterministic function of observed data. 

In terms of just the Stan code here are a few points:

1) Since both Y and N1 are declared as data then you can create N2 in the transformed data block rather than the transformed parameters block (transformed parameters is for functions of parameters, so in this case that would only be for functions of lambda):

transformed data {
 int N2;
 N2 <- N1 - Y[1];
}

You could also just compute N2 before calling Stan and also pass that in as data since its just a function of Y and N1, which are both data. 

2) Since lambda is a probability and thus constrained to be between 0 and 1 it needs to be declared with <lower=0, upper=1>. Once you do that you can drop the uniform(0,1) since a parameter declared with <lower=0,upper=1> will get a uniform(0,1) prior by default if you don't specify one. (Alternatively, there's a binomial_logit function that will let you declare lambda on the logit scale (with no constraints) and will do the inverse_logit transformation for you. Although the estimates for lambda would then be on the logit scale).

Best, 

Jonah
